name: motion_graphs
description: Linked kinematics graphs of one straight-line motion: position x(t), velocity v(t), acceleration a(t) stacked on ONE shared time axis (pick the panels), the object on a track above, and a time cursor through every panel — a dot on each graph, tangents showing slope of x = v and slope of v = a, the values read out beside each panel. Choose it for ANY question about motion graphs: how x–t, v–t and a–t relate, slope = velocity, area under v–t = displacement/distance, speeding up, braking, uniform acceleration, a car or ball moving in 1D. Motion: constant acceleration {x0, v0, a, duration}, or `segments` [{duration, a}] (or v1, the velocity at the piece's end); position is continuous. `t` is the cursor's time and ANIMATES: {"animate": {"t": 6}, "duration": 4} runs the object, cursor, readouts and shading — SET t in params (e.g. 0) first. shade "to_cursor" fills the area under v(t) up to the cursor (it grows as t sweeps; above the axis yellow, below red). Paused, the viewer drags the cursor (its t pill, or anywhere on the graphs), drags a v piece up/down (near an end: that corner's velocity; the middle: the whole piece), an a piece (its acceleration), and scrubs or taps the header numbers — everything follows; an explore beat naming nothing invites this. Numbers for text: {motion.t}, {motion.x}, {motion.v}, {motion.a} (at the cursor), {motion.displacement}, {motion.distance} (0 to the cursor), {motion.displacement_total}, {motion.distance_total}, {motion.x_end}, {motion.v_end}, {motion.duration}, {motion.a_<i>}, {motion.v_<i>} (piece i's a and end velocity). `{data: [t, v]}` lands on the v–t graph.

duration.description: How long the motion lasts (no segments). Default 5.

v1.description: Instead of a: the velocity at the piece's end.

v0.description: Only for an instant change of velocity (a bounce) at this piece's start; leave it out for a smooth motion.

label.description: A word or three naming the phase ("braking"), written above it.

segments.description: The motion in pieces of constant acceleration, in order: e.g. [{duration: 2, a: 2}, {duration: 3}, {duration: 2, v1: 0}] speeds up, cruises, brakes to a stop. At most 8.

panels.description: Which graphs, drawn top to bottom x, v, a (default all three), e.g. ["x", "v"].

t.description: The cursor's time (default 0). Animate it to run the motion.

cursor.description: Draw the time cursor, dots, tangents and readouts (default true).

track.description: Draw the object on a position track above the graphs (default true).

shade.description: Shade the area under v(t): up to the cursor, over the whole motion, or none (default).

tangents.description: Tangents at the cursor on x(t) (slope = v) and v(t) (slope = a). Default true.

readout.description: x, v, a at the cursor written beside each panel (default true).

numbers.description: The motion's numbers in a header line, scrubbable: true = v0 and a (constant acceleration; the default there) or v0 (segments; off by default there); or a list.

units.description: Units of position and time (default m, s); v and a take x/t and x/t².

labels.description: The graphs' symbols (default x, v, a, t) and a name for the object.

x_range.description: [min, max] of the x panel (default: round numbers that hold the motion).

element_ids.axes_x / axes_v / axes_a: a panel's axes (value axis, t axis at 0); its ticks_<k>, label_<k>, unit_<k> come with it
element_ids.label_x / label_v / label_a / label_t: a graph's symbol; label_t the time caption
element_ids.time_ticks: the time numbers under the bottom panel
element_ids.v_seg_<i> / a_seg_<i>: piece i of v(t) / a(t) (constant case: piece 0)
element_ids.curve_v / curve_a: SET — the whole v(t) / a(t) graph
element_ids.cursor: the time cursor; drawing it brings its dots, tangents, readouts and handle
element_ids.cursor_knob / readout_t: the cursor's handle and the time in it
element_ids.dot_x / dot_v / dot_a: a graph's point at the cursor
element_ids.tangent_x / tangent_v: the tangent at the cursor (slope of x = v, of v = a)
element_ids.readout_x / readout_v / readout_a: x, v, a at the cursor
element_ids.track / track_label: the position track and its caption
element_ids.object: the moving object (object_arrow, its velocity, and object_label come with it)
element_ids.object_arrow / object_label: its velocity arrow (absent at v ≈ 0) and its name
element_ids.name_x0 / name_v0 / name_a / unit_x0 / u: a header number's name and unit
element_ids.title: the title, when set

examples.request: Show the position, velocity and acceleration graphs of a ball thrown upward.
A car speeds up, cruises, then brakes: how do its x–t, v–t and a–t graphs fit together?
Why is the area under a velocity graph the distance travelled?
